name: Vasishteswarar Temple, Thenkudithittai
deity: Shiva as Vasishteswarar, with the goddess Loganayaki
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine of the Kaveri delta near Thanjavur, sung in the Tevaram (7th century)
summary: At Thenkudithittai near Thanjavur, Shiva is Vasishteswarar, worshipped by the sage Vasishta; the temple is revered as a Guru sthalam, with a drop of water said to fall on the linga every naazhigai.

sections.history: Thenkudithittai is a Kaveri-delta village near Thanjavur, set on a mound between the Vennar and Vettaru rivers, and its temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam counted among the shrines sung in the Tevaram on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The Lord is worshipped as Vasishteswarar, named for the sage Vasishta who is said to have worshipped here, and the goddess as Loganayaki. The shrine was built and endowed in stone under the Cholas and their successors, and it has long been revered as a Guru sthalam, a place of the planet Jupiter, drawing those who seek the grace of the preceptor of the gods.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian delta manner, with a gopuram, pillared halls and a prakara around the sanctum of Vasishteswarar. The goddess Loganayaki has her own shrine, and between the two stands a distinct, separately-roofed shrine for Guru, Jupiter, which devotees say is unusual among Guru sthalams, where the planet is more often honoured in the Dakshinamurthy form. A south-facing Dakshinamurthy shrine is also present, as at other delta temples.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that the sage Vasishta, preceptor of the solar line, worshipped Shiva here and that the Lord took his name as Vasishteswarar. The place is also tied to the pralaya, the great flood, when this mound between the rivers is said to have stayed dry, giving the village its name of the southern settlement on the mound. A continual drop of water is said to fall upon the linga at each naazhigai, a wonder devotees come to witness.
sections.festivals: As a Guru sthalam the temple keeps special worship on the transit days of Jupiter from one zodiac sign to the next, and on Thursdays, the day of Guru. Maha Shivaratri, the monthly Pradosham, and the Tamil month festivals are also observed. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally.
sections.experience: Many come to Thenkudithittai as a Guru sthalam, to worship Jupiter in his own shrine and to pray for learning and good counsel, before worshipping Vasishteswarar and Loganayaki. The temple keeps the calm of a delta village sanctuary near Thanjavur, and the ceaseless water-drop on the linga is among the quiet wonders devotees recall.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thenkudithittai lies on a mound between the Vennar and Vettaru rivers, a short distance from Thanjavur in the Kaveri delta. Thanjavur is the nearest major railway station; Tiruchirappalli airport is about 65 km away. Local buses and autos reach the village.
